name: Ill-conditioned blending
blurb: Coefficients spanning eight orders of magnitude — built to break a solver's numerics.

name: Refinery crude blending
blurb: A small refinery choosing how much of each crude to buy and how to route it through the units, subject to product quality specs.

name: Degenerate transport
blurb: A transportation model with massive primal degeneracy — built to stall a naive ratio test.

name: Refinery blend — impossible spec
blurb: A volume target and a sulfur specification that cannot both be met. The solver refuses it with a proof, then names the constraints in conflict.

name: Supply chain flow
blurb: Multi-echelon flow from sources through hubs to demand points.

name: Refinery crude blending — planner size
blurb: The same problem an order of magnitude larger — the size a planner actually runs.

name: Production planning
blurb: Multi-period production, inventory and backlog across a plant network.

name: Production planning — full horizon
blurb: Forty units, thirty products, thirty-six periods. Around thirty thousand simplex iterations: long enough to watch the primal box sit lit while the log scrolls.

name: Production smoothing
blurb: Running a unit up and down costs money, so the objective penalises the period-to-period change quadratically. The Hessian is the singular tridiagonal second-difference matrix.

name: Factor-model risk
blurb: Minimise x'Σx − μ'x over a budget and position limits, Σ built as a factor model. Takes the interior-point path and then crossover, because normal equations go dense the moment Q is not diagonal.

name: Unit commitment — half day
blurb: Which generators to switch on, and how hard to run them. Binary on/off decisions.

name: Unit commitment — the cuts demo
blurb: Solve it, then untick cut separation and solve it again. Same objective; one node against fifty-one. This is the model to show.

name: Unit commitment — a full day, 14 units
blurb: Cuts close part of the gap and the tree does the rest: a few thousand nodes, proven optimal. The branch-and-bound box stays lit and the bound and incumbent close on each other while you watch.

name: Refinery scheduling — a shift
blurb: Which mode each unit runs in each slot, what it charges, and what sits in the tanks between. Mode changes cost money, a mode entered has to be held, and a unit is off or above turndown — never between. This is the layer under the planning LP.

name: Refinery scheduling — a week
blurb: Six units, three modes, twelve slots, 432 binaries. Yields depend on the mode, which is exactly what a fixed-yield planning LP cannot express. CPLEX and Gurobi both confirm the answer; watch how much of the gap the cuts take before the tree starts.

name: Process optimization (RTO)
blurb: The real-time-optimization layer: move each unit's operating point along its measured gain matrix to hit product targets at least utility cost. Compressor power really does go as the square of throughput. A third of the controlled variables carry a spec band but no target, so the Hessian is singular on purpose.

name: Haverly pooling — the counterexample
blurb: Three crudes, one pool whose sulfur is a DECISION, two products with sulfur specs. Quality times flow is a product of two variables, so the model is nonconvex and the obvious linear version of it reports a blend that cannot be made. Solved to proven global optimality; the published answer is 400 and this is the instance that shows why a local method is not enough — started from random points it lands on 100 a quarter of the time.

name: Refinery pooling — two pools
blurb: The same physics at planner scale: five crudes, two pools with free qualities, three products. Cheap crude is high-sulfur crude, so the blend ratio is the whole decision. Watch the spatial branch-and-bound box: it splits a CONTINUOUS variable's range, which is the step a mixed-integer tree has no analogue for.

name: Cardinality-constrained portfolio
blurb: Quadratic risk over continuous weights, binaries deciding which names are held at all, at most five. Every node relaxation is a QP — there is no simplex tableau to read a Gomory cut off, which is why this path has no cut box.

name: Discrete lot blending
blurb: Components arrive as whole tanker lots, and the blend is judged by squared deviation from spec. Rounding the continuous optimum gives the wrong answer; so does optimising the linear part and evaluating the quadratic there — that second one was a live bug here until an instance like this caught it.
